title: LIN-4263 tidy-after: one posting-key list and one dispatch order (the edges its blind reads named)
description:
## Goal

The rules LIN-4263 re-wrote are back to one copy each: one list of the keys that identify a posting row, and one rule for the order of a lineage's dispatches.

## Context

Two independent blind reads of LIN-4263 (`6ff38cf5c`, `/cost` per-dispatch breakdown) both scored it "mixed", for the same two copies at its edges:

* `postingKeysOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`) repeats `isPostingRow`'s `[id, _id, loopId]` list in the same file, and neither uses the other;
* `rankOf` and its sort copy the private dispatch order in `lib/lineage-membership.js`, but without its tie handling, so two undated members give `Infinity - Infinity = NaN` and the order is undefined.

This is the first trial of the loop's "after" step: when a blind read names the copies a change left at its edges, they become a small tidy-after in the same area, straight away.

## This step

Each rule ends with one owner, and the copy is deleted in the same change. `dispatchesOf` reuses the existing order, exported rather than re-written, so it picks up the tie handling, and the existing key list. No change to any `/cost` figure.

**Not this ticket:** anything else in `/cost`; the label question (founder versus cost-dominant model).

## Done when

* `postingKeysOf` and `rankOf` are gone, or are thin re-uses of the owners.
* A test with two undated members in one lineage gives a defined order, and it is red at `6ff38cf5c`.
* `/cost` output for LIN-4263's fixtures is unchanged.

## Report back

What was deleted, what the owners now export, and anything else at this edge that a blind read would count.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began). This corrects "Done when"

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 13:42, at `6ff38cf5c`) checked the NaN claim and found it isn't a live bug. ECMAScript's SortCompare turns a NaN result into `+0`, and `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so two undated members already keep their input order, exactly as `byDispatchOrder` does ("ties keep input order"). **So "red at** `6ff38cf5c`**" can't be met honestly, and the second Done-when is replaced** (the person's call). The defect is that there are two copies, not that the order is wrong. Say that in the report, and don't contrive a red. In order:

1. **One dispatch order.** Export the order from `lib/lineage-membership.js` (it stays a leaf) and have `dispatchesOf` use it, either by sorting the member rows and then mapping, or by comparing `entry.member`. Don't add a third "entry" comparator. Delete `rankOf` and its sort. The module header gains "dispatch order" in its list of what it decides. **The test pins the rule where it lives:** a unit test on the exported order (undated last, ties keep input order). It passes before and after, and goes red if the rule is re-forked.
2. **One posting-key list.** `postingKeysOf` is the owner, and `isPostingRow(row, id)` becomes `postingKeysOf(row).includes(id)`, with the same coercion and null filter.
3. **Decide about** `keyOf` (`id ?? _id`, the same file), a third, narrower key reader. `dispatchesOf` emits `itemId: keyOf(member)` but matches on `postingKeysOf`, so a row known only by `loopId` would report `itemId: null`. Either derive it from the same owner, or say in a line why it's a different rule. `anchorOf` (a lineage key, not a posting key) stays, with a one-line comment saying so.
4. `/cost` **unchanged:** `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/` goldens and `expected-changes.json` untouched, plus `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js` green before and after.

**Not in this ticket:** `lib/dispatch-lineage.js:162`'s marker sort (the same shape, different rows, not `/cost`; list it as a follow-up); moving the per-dispatch split into its own module.

## Done when (replaces the list above)

* `rankOf` is gone, and `postingKeysOf` is the one key list (`keyOf` derived or explained).
* The exported order has its own test.
* `/cost`'s goldens are untouched.

---

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out: the plan was implemented as approved; the full text is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.*

**Implemented:** PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2300](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2300>), squash-merged as `473cc865`. `byDispatchOrder` is exported from `lib/lineage-membership.js` and `dispatchesOf` reuses it (`rankOf` and its sort deleted); `postingKeysOf` is the one posting-key list, `isPostingRow` is a membership test on it and `keyOf` is `postingKeysOf(row)[0] ?? null`; `anchorOf` keeps its own rule, with a comment. `/cost` goldens and `expected-changes.json` untouched. Deviation: review found three of the guards did not go red under a real re-fork, so close-out added three witnesses (tests only, commit `9907839a`). The `dispatch-lineage.js:162` / `recent-runs.js:46` follow-up is LIN-4278.

### Session fit and review

fits one session

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4276 @ 6ff38cf5c

Read at LinearViewer `origin/main` = `6ff38cf5c`, which is LIN-4263 itself, so "red at 6ff38cf5c" means red at base.

### Why this will be difficult: the second Done-when cannot honestly go red

The ticket says `rankOf`'s sort gives `Infinity - Infinity = NaN` for two undated members, "and the order is undefined". The NaN part is true. The undefined order is not. In ECMAScript, SortCompare turns a NaN comparator result into `+0`, and `Array.prototype.sort` has been stable since ES2019. So two undated entries compare as equal and keep their input order. That is exactly what the owner does: `byDispatchOrder` returns `x === y ? 0`, and `lineage-membership.js:62` says "ties keep input order". I checked on Node v25.9.0 with 2, 5, 11, 20 and 50 entries, a third of them undated. The undated entries always came out in input order and after every dated one.

`dispatchesOf` (`lib/cost-read.js:462`) sorts `[...record.members, ...record.missing]`. `members` is already in owner order, `missing` is disjoint, and both comparators treat an undated pair as a tie. So the output is identical today, and a test asserting a defined order for two undated members is **green at base**. Its own rule says it must be red. Expect the worker either to invent a contrived red (calling a private comparator directly, or relying on an "unstable sort" claim) or to stall. **First move: correct the Done-when before work starts.** The honest version is "the test pins the order, and it guards the reuse". It passes before and after, and goes red only if someone re-forks the rule. The real reason to do the tidy is still sound: one owner, so the two can't drift. It isn't a live bug.

### The mechanical parts are small but have a shape trap

- **Order:** export `byDispatchOrder`. It takes rows (`row.dispatchedAt`), while `dispatchesOf` sorts wrapper entries (`entry.at`). Either sort the member rows with the owner and map afterwards, or use `(a, b) => byDispatchOrder(a.member, b.member)`. Don't add a second "entry" comparator. `lineage-membership.js` is a declared leaf module that imports only `utils/time.js`, and exporting from it keeps it a leaf. `cost-read.js:37` already imports from it.
- **Keys:** make `postingKeysOf` the owner and write `isPostingRow(row, id)` as `postingKeysOf(row).includes(id)`. Same `String` coercion and null filter, so no figure moves. Tie order matters a little here, because `byPostingKey` is first-wins, which is one more reason the order must not change.

### What a blind read would still count at this edge

1. **`keyOf`** (`cost-read.js:48`, `id ?? _id`) is a third row-identity list in the same file. `dispatchesOf` emits `itemId: keyOf(member)` but matches on `postingKeysOf`, which adds `loopId`. A row known only by `loopId` matches records but reports `itemId: null`. Decide whether this is the same rule or a different one. Don't leave it unexplained.
2. **`anchorOf`** (`lineage-membership.js:27`, `rootItemId || _id || id`) is a fourth id-shape list. It is legitimately different (anchor, not posting key), but it is worth a one-line comment saying so.
3. **`latestDispatchedBy`** skips undated entries but relies on the array already being in dispatch order. That is fine once the sort is owned. Mention it in the docstring.
4. The name `rankOf` also exists in `lib/task-board-view.js:165`. That one is unrelated and not a copy, so a grep-based "gone" check should be scoped to `cost-read.js`.

The "/cost output unchanged" check is cheap. `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js` (19 tests) is the fixture set to rerun before and after.

## Survey global: LIN-4276 @ 6ff38cf5c

**Where it lands.** `lib/cost-read.js` (759 lines) and `lib/lineage-membership.js` (88-line leaf, imports only `utils/time.js`). Over LIN-4177 → 4179 → 4201 → 4226 the cost read has been pulling toward one owner per decision: its header names which module decides what ("restated nowhere here"), and `cost-read-census.test.js` polices who imports the fold helpers. LIN-4263 broke that pattern in two small places: about 40 lines of private helpers next to `dispatchesOf`, one of which restates a rule the header says lives in `lineage-membership.js`. The trend is still good, and this ticket is the right size to repair it.

**A premise to check first: the `NaN` is not a live bug.** ECMAScript's SortCompare turns a `NaN` comparator result into `+0`, and `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so `rankOf(a) - rankOf(b)` already keeps two undated entries in input order. That is exactly what `byDispatchOrder` does. On node v25.9.0, sorting `[null,5,null,null,1]` with it gives `5,2,1,3,4`, and the same holds at 40 elements. So "a test with two undated members … red at `6ff38cf5c`" probably can't be met honestly. The real defect is that there are two copies, not that the order is wrong. Worth saying in the report rather than writing a test that is red for some other reason.

**Done the obvious way:**
- Export `byDispatchOrder` (or a `sortByDispatchOrder(rows)`) from `lineage-membership.js`. Its key reads `row.dispatchedAt`, but `dispatchesOf` sorts `{member, at}` wrappers. So either sort the members before mapping, or compare on `entry.member`. Don't add a third adapter. The module's header lists what it decides; it should gain "dispatch order" as a line. The census needs no change, since a new export isn't a listed fold helper.
- Keep one key list. The natural owner is `postingKeysOf`, with `isPostingRow = postingKeysOf(row).includes(itemId)`. Both are private to one file, so nothing outside has to learn anything.
- "Unchanged `/cost` output" already has a guard: `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/goldens-lin4197.json` plus `expected-changes.json`. A run that leaves `expected-changes.json` untouched is the proof.

**What a blind read would still count at this edge:**
- `keyOf` (`id ?? _id`, same file) is a third, narrower key reader. `dispatchesOf` emits `itemId: keyOf(member)`, so a member matched only by `loopId` would report `itemId: null`. Either explain the narrower list where it's used or derive it from the same owner.
- `anchorOf` (`rootItemId || _id || id`) is a different rule: it gives a lineage key, not a posting key. Leave it, but don't fold it in.
- `lib/dispatch-lineage.js:162` uses the same `(x ?? Infinity) - (y ?? Infinity)` sort for ticket markers. It's another copy of the dispatch order, outside `/cost`.

**Better, and affordable here:** the two deletions, a one-line owner note in each header, and a unit test on the exported order itself: undated members last, ties keep input order. That test pins the rule where it lives instead of through `dispatchesOf`.

**Better still, not this ticket's:** moving `dispatch-lineage.js`'s marker sort onto the same order. Its rows carry `dispatched`, not `dispatchedAt`, and it isn't `/cost`. More broadly: `cost-read.js` now holds the per-dispatch split (rule C, `latestDispatchedBy`, `dispatchesOf`). That could become its own module beside `request-usage-fold.js` once a second reader wants it.

## LIN-4276 implemented: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2300

Commit `6e5320a7` on `feat/lin-4276-one-posting-key-and-dispatch-order`. CI is green on the PR: `CI success`, Unit tests, all four E2E shards, and Secret scan (source).

- **One dispatch order:** `byDispatchOrder` is exported from `lib/lineage-membership.js`. `dispatchesOf` reuses it, and `rankOf` is deleted. The NaN was never live, so the order is pinned by a test, not a red.
- **One posting-key list:** `postingKeysOf` is the owner. `isPostingRow` is a membership test on it, and `keyOf` derives from it. `anchorOf` stays a separate lineage key, with a comment.
- **`/cost` goldens and `expected-changes.json` are untouched.** One edge changes: a row with a `loopId` but no `id` or `_id` was listed twice, and now is listed once. That is recorded in the PR.
- Unit suite: 23,598 of 23,598 pass. One baseline failure (`LIN-4104 D2`, `db-indexes.test.js`) did not reproduce.

## Review — LIN-4276

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2300 at head `6e5320a70fb64a514ccad7a20eb76c0e82ca2812` (base `origin/main` `6ff38cf5`; main has since gained `6d287518` LIN-4270, which is unrelated, and the PR is still MERGEABLE).

CI: green on `6e5320a7`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed.

### Scope and plan match
The diff touches only the plan's places: `lib/cost-read.js`, `lib/lineage-membership.js`, and three test files. `tests/fixtures/` is untouched, so the goldens and `expected-changes.json` did not move (`git diff --stat origin/main...pr2300 -- tests/fixtures` is empty). Every plan step is done:
- `byDispatchOrder` is exported, and the module header gains "dispatch order".
- `dispatchesOf` sorts rows with the owner, then maps them to entries. It has no entry comparator.
- `rankOf` is deleted.
- `postingKeysOf` is moved up and owns the list. `isPostingRow` is a membership test on it, and `keyOf` is `postingKeysOf(row)[0] ?? null`.
- `anchorOf` has a comment saying it is a lineage key, not a posting key.
- `latestDispatchedBy`'s docstring now says entries must already be in dispatch order.

The report says the NaN was never live. Regression check: `cost-read.js` and `lineage-membership.js` have had no commits since the ticket was created other than this PR. The recent history (4147 → 4263) has no reverts, and this PR re-applies nothing that was reverted.

### Independent runs (mine, not the author's)
I ran 10 cost-read test files (161 tests): the census, lin-4147, lin-4263, the lin4197 replay and corpus goldens, the lin-4201 replay change list, cost-read, agreement, kpi-path and outcome-sets.
- **PR head:** 161/161 pass.
- **Base lib with the PR's tests:** 6 fail, all of them the new LIN-4276 tests (the census re-fork guard ×2, `byDispatchOrder` ×3 for the missing export, and the loopId-only member). The goldens and replay are green on both sides, so `/cost` figures are unchanged for the fixtures.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards; tree clean at `6e5320a7`)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `byDispatchOrder` flipped | 35 fail ✅ |
| `keyOf` back to `id ?? _id` (base) | the loopId-only test is red ✅ |
| `isPostingRow` restored to its own `[row?.id, row?._id, row?.loopId]` literal | census key-list test is red ✅ |
| **`.sort(byDispatchOrder)` removed from `dispatchesOf`** | only the existing LIN-4263 out-of-window test goes red. **The new "two undated and two dated members" test stays green.** Every member in it is fetched, so `record.members` is already in owner order from `groupLineageMembership`, and the test never reaches `dispatchesOf`'s own sort. Its docstring says it pins the order `dispatchesOf` reuses, and it does not. |
| **Re-fork as an anonymous `(toEpochMs(a.dispatchedAt) ?? Infinity) - …` comparator** (no `rankOf` name, import kept) | **all green**. The census only looks for the name `rankOf`. |
| **`isPostingRow` narrowed to `[row?.id, row?._id]` (loopId dropped, written differently)** | **all green**, including run-view, lin-4201 records-first and cost-callers (95 more tests). No behavioural test exercises the loopId shape of the one key list, and the census regex only matches the exact literal. |

These three gaps are why the verdict is conditional. Each one is a witness for a claim this ticket makes ("one owner, and a re-fork fails a test"). I wrote all three probes below and ran them: each passes at `6e5320a7` and goes red under its mutation (A red under removed-sort; B red under narrowed `isPostingRow`; C red under removed-sort and anonymous re-fork).

### Production-row check for the `keyOf` edge
The only behaviour change is for a row with `loopId` but neither `id` nor `_id`. Every production caller of `readCost`/`lineageRecords` (`routes/proxy-compute.js:735`, `lib/kpi-stats.js:1087`, `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js:181`, `lib/effort-readout.js:444`, `lib/model-routing-history.js:37`) passes dispatch-store docs. The run page's loop rows (loopId-shaped) reach the cost read only through `lineageFigureOf` → `lineageUsageOf`, which never calls `keyOf`/`distinctRows`. So no live input reaches the changed edge.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "an undated-last dispatch-time sort written outside `lineage-membership.js`". Siblings:
- `lib/dispatch-lineage.js:162` (marker sort on `dispatched`) and `lib/recent-runs.js:46-47` (on `at`): **outside**. They are not `/cost`, sort different row shapes, and the ticket and plan carve them out. Close-out files one follow-up for them after checking it doesn't already exist.
- `lib/task-board-view.js:165` `rankOf`: not a copy (unrelated).

The class "posting-row key list" has no other copy in `lib/` (`loopId` now appears in `cost-read.js` only in `postingKeysOf`).

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (bounded class: one dispatch order, reused by `dispatchesOf`). The new order test does not exercise `dispatchesOf`'s sort. **Before the merge**, close-out adds to `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js`, in the LIN-4276 describe (replacing or alongside "two undated and two dated members"), a case where the sort itself decides the order: fetched `[u1]` (undated), identity `[d3, u1, u2]` (`d3` dated 3h ago, `u2` undated), one record on `d3`, `perDispatch`. Expect `itemId`s `['d3','u1','u2']`. The distinguishing condition: it goes red when `.sort(byDispatchOrder)` is removed (unsorted it gives `['u1','d3','u2']`). Also correct that test's docstring so it doesn't claim to pin `dispatchesOf`'s order if it is kept as is.
- **Inside** (bounded class: one dispatch order, the re-fork guard). The census misses a re-fork under another name. **Before the merge**, close-out extends the LIN-4276 census describe in `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js` to also assert `/\.sort\(byDispatchOrder\)/` matches `lib/cost-read.js` and `/\?\?\s*Infinity/` does not. The file's only other `Infinity` is `?? -Infinity` at :359 (window filter), which this regex does not match. The distinguishing condition: it goes red under the anonymous `?? Infinity` comparator mutation.
- **Inside** (bounded class: one posting-key list, which `isPostingRow` must use). No behavioural test covers the `loopId` key through `isPostingRow`, so a narrowed rewrite passes everything. **Before the merge**, close-out adds a case (lin-4263 file, importing `lineageFigureOf` from `lib/cost-read.js`): rows `[{loopId:'L1', rootItemId:'b1', dispatchedAt: at(5), feedback: []}, {loopId:'L2', rootItemId:'b1', dispatchedAt: at(2), feedback: []}]`, records `[request('b1','L1','q1',4,{costUsd:0.4})]`. Expect `lineageFigureOf(...).lastIndex === 0`. The distinguishing condition: it goes red (`1`) when `isPostingRow` drops `loopId`.
- **Inside** (`keyOf` derived from the one list): no live row has `loopId` without `id`/`_id`. **Discharged** by this review's caller read above (all `fetchedRows` come from the dispatch store; the run page's loop rows bypass `keyOf`).
- **Outside**: `lib/dispatch-lineage.js:162` and `lib/recent-runs.js:46-47` re-write the undated-last sort. Close-out files one follow-up ("check whether these should take `byDispatchOrder`") after a duplicate check. This does not block the merge.

After adding the three witnesses, close-out re-runs the 10-file set above (expect 164/164) and waits for CI to be green on the new head before merging.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The refactor is correct and complete, `/cost` goldens are unchanged, and CI is green, but three of the claimed "re-fork fails a test" guards don't go red under a real re-fork. Close-out adds the three named witnesses (tests only, no lib change).

## Close-out — LIN-4276

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2300, squash-merged as `473cc865` (pinned with `--match-head-commit 9907839a`). Deploy landed: harbour.cat footer shows `473cc865`. Review's verdict was Approve, conditional on the ledger; all of it is settled below.

### Changes I made after approval
One commit, `9907839a`, tests only, no `lib/` change. Each answers a "What CI Did Not Prove" line of the review:
1. `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js`: new case where `dispatchesOf`'s own sort decides the order (fetched `[u1]`, identity `[d3, u1, u2]`; expects `['d3','u1','u2']`, unsorted gives `['u1','d3','u2']`). The docstring that claimed the old undated test pins `dispatchesOf`'s sort is corrected.
2. `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js`: asserts `.sort(byDispatchOrder)` is in `lib/cost-read.js` and `/\?\?\s*Infinity/` is not.
3. `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js`: `lineageFigureOf` on two loopId-only rows with a record under `L1`; expects `lastIndex === 0`.

### Ledger
* **Inside, dispatchesOf sort not exercised:** done (1). Mutation: removing `.sort(byDispatchOrder)` now fails the new case plus the census case and the existing out-of-window test (3 fail).
* **Inside, census misses an anonymous re-fork:** done (2). Mutation: an anonymous `(toEpochMs(a.dispatchedAt) ?? Infinity) - …` comparator fails the census case.
* **Inside, no behavioural test for loopId through isPostingRow:** done (3). Mutation: `isPostingRow` narrowed to `[id, _id]` fails the new case (1 fail). Each mutation was reverted; `lib/` is as the PR had it.
* **Inside, keyOf edge:** discharged by review's production-caller read (no live row reaches it); I did not re-derive it.
* **Outside:** `lib/dispatch-lineage.js:162` and `lib/recent-runs.js:46-47`: filed as LIN-4278 (Low, labels `kind:follow-up` and `Improvement`, related to this ticket). A search for the same files and finding turned up no existing ticket.

### CI and verification
* The 10-file cost-read set: 164/164 on the PR head, and 164/164 again on merged `main` (`473cc865`). `tests/fixtures` is unchanged from `6ff38cf5`.
* CI on `9907839a`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed, read again before the merge. CI on `main` at `473cc865` also completed with success.
* Not run: a live `/cost` check on the deployed instance (needs a signed-in workspace session, which I don't have). The change is a refactor with unchanged goldens, so the tests above are my evidence. Anyone with a session can open `/cost` for a lineage with a follow-up and compare.
* No post-deploy steps or named monitor were on the ledger.

### Description
Archived first (snapshot captured 14:28:41Z, verified to hold the full pre-prune description), then the Implementation Plan body was replaced by a stub. The problem statement, Done-when, the Survey section, and the `Implementation Plan` heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due: no` lines are kept.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The edits were not difficult: about 20 lines. The work bound on `keyOf`. It feeds `distinctRows`, `fetchedKeys` and `missing`, and through `missing` it feeds `incomplete`. My first red test failed for a different reason than I expected (`requests` was 2, not 1). Chasing that showed that a `loopId`-only row was listed twice: once as fetched and once as missing. That second listing can null `totalUsd`, so the real defect was deeper than the reported `itemId`. The witness discipline was the other friction. The order rule can't honestly go red. The `byDispatchOrder` pin is red on base only because the export is missing (`sort(undefined)` falls back to string order, and one case passes by accident). I used a namespace import so the rest of that file still loads on base.

**2. What I'd do first.** Run one `loopId`-only fixture through `readCostOverRecords` before planning. It shows `keyOf`'s reach in one call.

**3. What I'd tidy.** The re-fork guard in the census is a regex over source text, so a reformat slips past it. A behavioural guard would be sturdier. `postingKeysOf` and `keyOf` are a row-identity rule, but they live inside the cost read. And `dispatchesOf` with `latestDispatchedBy` (the per-dispatch split) wants its own module.

**4. The ticket, if the area were how I'd want it.** Row identity (posting keys) would sit next to `anchorOf` as an exported rule, with order beside it. Then LIN-4263 would have imported both, and this ticket wouldn't exist. At most it would be "dispatchesOf uses the two owners": ten lines, with no `keyOf` decision to make.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.** The NaN claim, which the Surveys already corrected. The plan framed the `keyOf` change as an `itemId` and dedupe edge. Its real reach is `missing`, then `incomplete`, then `totalUsd`, which is a figure for that row shape. The plan said the order pin "passes before and after", but it can't, because the export it tests doesn't exist on base. The plan named key order as a top risk but had no witness for it. Mutation showed the existing suite doesn't catch putting `loopId` first, so I added a pin.

**6. What it left behind.** `byDispatchOrder` is a new public export of a leaf module. Two sorts of the same shape (`dispatch-lineage.js:162` and `recent-runs.js:46-47`) don't know about it. `postingKeysOf` is private, so no other reader of row ids can learn the rule. Simpler now: one key list, a one-line `isPostingRow`, no `rankOf`, and the `loopId`-only double listing is gone. I don't know whether that row shape occurs in production. The census now also polices a text pattern.

**7. Was a separate tidy-after worth it?** Barely, on cost. Two Surveys, a plan, a ~9-minute CI run and a review around a 20-line change is mostly overhead. Inside LIN-4263 it would have been cheaper, because the author already held the context. But the separate pass found the double listing, which a quick in-PR tidy would probably have missed. What would have made it smaller: checking the NaN claim before filing, which would have avoided the Done-when rewrite, and a census rule that flags a private helper restating a rule an imported module owns. That rule would have stopped the copies in LIN-4263 itself.

issue.title: Two undated-last dispatch-time sorts re-state byDispatchOrder (dispatch-lineage.js:162, recent-runs.js:46)
